text:
Nina P: quick follow-up to the quant profiles thread. i'm proposing a hysteresis-based activation quant gating approach that uses per-layer thresholds to avoid flip-flopping and to localize rollbacks when a layer misbehaves. idea is lightweight and can be toggled per-model.

Omar L: can you sketch the high level? how is hysteresis different from the warmup token idea?

Nina P: warmup is time-based (first N tokens). hysteresis is quality-signal based with momentum: a layer only switches to low-bit activation if its running degscore stays below T_low for K consecutive eval steps, and it only switches back to high-bit if degscore exceeds T_high for L consecutive steps. T_high > T_low to add hysteresis.

Sam J: per-layer thresholds sounds fiddly. do we need to expose those to customers?

Nina P: default: no. we ship sensible model heuristics (per-model manifest) and expose a simplified fidelity toggle: hysteresis: on|off, sensitivity: low|medium|high. advanced tenants can override per-layer numbers in Dedicated/Private.

Rae T: runtime implementation note: we'll compute per-layer degscore during shadow runs and maintain a tiny rolling buffer per inference shard. need to ensure this doesn't add locking in hot paths. make it lock-free ring buffers and aggregate in the worker thread.

Omar L: what do we measure as degscore at layer granularity? token-likelihood drift? residual-norm change?

Nina P: proposal: two signals per layer: (A) residual-scale deviation (L2 ratio vs baseline), (B) per-layer token-likelihood delta after the layer output (approximated via a small probe head). combine into a weighted degscore. weights and thresholds come from offline calibration.

Sam J: hmm the probe head adds compute. can it be cheap?

Nina P: yes, probe head is tiny (1-2 linear layers) and we only run it on sampled tokens (1/10th of tokens for production). it's for telemetry and gating, not inference final scoring.

Omar L: failure modes? sounds like we could end up with many layers toggling independently and odd inconsistencies.

Nina P: to mitigate: two constraints: (1) global rollback policy: if >X% of layers toggle back to high within a short window, force whole-model high-fidelity, and (2) inter-layer consistency checks that disallow toggling of early-layer to low-bit if downstream layers are still high-bit for a head-sensitive model. both are heuristic but conservative.

Rae T: telemetry-wise we'll emit events: layer_id, prev_mode, new_mode, trigger_signal, probe_sample_rate, and backlog memory delta. ops-bot should create canary for the telemetry stream.

ops-bot: canary scheduled: hysteresis-quant-probe-2026-03-26. will report to #eng-sre. :robot_face:

Sam J: API sketch? keep it simple for customers. maybe:

```
{"fidelity": {"activation_mode": "hysteresis|deferred|always|never", "sensitivity": "medium", "sample_rate": 0.1}}
```

Nina P: yep. internally we expand sensitivity -> per-layer thresholds. also add `max_layer_toggles_per_minute` to avoid flapping.

Omar L: rollout plan? P0 should be purely shadow first.

Nina P: agreed. P0: shadow across a small fleet with detailed traces and no routing changes (collect degscore/probe). P1: shadow+metric-alerting (auto flag if any early-token regress). P2: canary 1% with automatic full-model fallback if global degscore > 1.25x baseline. P3: ramp.

Rae T: ops request: add a metric mapping for cost delta per toggle (because toggling back to high-bit increases memory/latency). SRE wants per-tenant delta in the canary dashboards.

Sam J: one more thought: per-layer hysteresis could be combined with deferred warmup for best of both worlds (warmup avoids early noise; hysteresis adapts later). we should test combination.

Nina P: agreed. P1 experiments include warmup+hysteresis combos. i'll draft a short RFC addendum with pseudocode for the hysteresis state machine and the probe sampling.

Omar L: i'll pair on the microbench to validate probe overhead and memory buffer costs.

Nina P: thanks everyone. i'll post the addendum and a small checklist for the canary. :spiral_notepad:
